rationale: The Latin anchors *repellere* (to drive back/repel) and *extorquere* (to wrest away/extort) point to a forcible sense of constraining or holding someone against their will, which aligns best with keep.v.21 ("hold and prevent from leaving"). While neither Latin term is a perfect match, the sense of forcible detention or restraint is closer to keep.v.21 than to prevent.v.02, and the Old English *a-nýdan* (to compel, force) supports a coercive holding/keeping sense.
